newsitem.title: ITALY: Stet vote won't affect sell-offs - Italy PM.
newsitem.headline: Stet vote won't affect sell-offs - Italy PM.

text.p: A suprise parliamentary defeat over the government's transfer of telecom holding Stet to the Treasury will not harm Italy's privatisation programme, Prime Minister Romano Prodi was quoted as saying on Thursday.
"With regard to the privatisation, nothing changes," Prodi was quoted as telling news agency ANSA while on his way to an official visit to Croatia.
The lower house of parliament dealt the government an unexpected blow late on Wednesday when it voted against the transfer of Stet from state holding IRI to the Treasury.

The government lost the motion by just four votes and many members of the coalition, including a number of ministers, failed to show up for the vote. "One could die laughing if you read the list of people who didn't vote," Prodi said.
He added that plans to merge Stet and the fixed-line telephone company, Telecom Italia would not be affected. "On a technical level nothing changes...there is no alarm," he told reporters.
"The only worry is that the affair could be interpreted badly by foreign investors," Prodi added.
And he said that IRI would be paid for the Stet holding regardless of the parliamentary setback. "Payment for the transfer of Stet shares is guaranteed," he said.
The Treasury said last month it would pay at least 14.53 trillion lire to debt-laden IRI to take over its controlling stake in STET.
Under a 1993 accord with the European Union, IRI has to cut its debt to below five trillion lire by the end of June from its end-1995 level of 22.5 trillion.

Prodi told AGI agency that he did not expect any problems from the European Commissioner for competition, Karel Van Miert, over the vote. Van Miert has been leading the Commission's drive to get IRI to reduce its debt level.
"I have known him for years and it will be easy for me to explain to him the truth of the matter," he said.
